title: would
subtitle: It would be nice.
summary: Use would for imagined situations now, would have done for imagined situations in the past, and would as the past of will, including for refusals and repeated past actions.

lesson.heading: Imagining a situation
lesson.text: We use **would ('d) / wouldn't** when we imagine a situation or action - something that is not real.

examples.text: **It would be** nice to buy a new car, but we can't afford it.
**I'd love** to live by the sea.
*A:* Shall I tell Chris what happened? *B:* No, **I wouldn't say** anything.
examples.note: = I wouldn't say anything in your situation

lesson.heading: would have (done)
lesson.text: We use **would have (done)** when we imagine something that didn't happen in the past.

examples.text: They helped us a lot. I don't know what **we'd have done** without their help.
examples.note: we'd have done = we would have done

examples.text: It's a shame you didn't see the film. **You would have liked** it.
I didn't tell Sam what happened. **He wouldn't have been** pleased.

lesson.heading: would (do) and would have (done)

left.label: now
examples: **I would call** Lisa, but I don't have her number.
I'm not going to invite them to the party. **They wouldn't come** anyway.

right.label: the past
examples: **I would have called** Lisa, but I didn't have her number.
I didn't invite them to the party. **They wouldn't have come** anyway.

lesson.note: We often use would in sentences with if: I would call Lisa if I had her number. / I would have called Lisa if I'd had her number.

left.label: will - it is possible
examples: **I'll stay** a little longer. I've got plenty of time.
**I'll call** Lisa. I have her number.

right.label: would - it isn't possible
examples: **I'd stay** a little longer, but I really have to go now.
**I'd call** Lisa, but I don't have her number.

lesson.heading: would as the past of will
rows: Tom said he'**d** call me on Sunday.
Amy promised that she **wouldn't** be late.
Lisa was annoyed because her car **wouldn't** start.

lesson.heading: wouldn't = refused to
lesson.text: **Somebody wouldn't do something** = he or she refused to do it.

examples.text: I tried to warn him, but **he wouldn't listen** to me.
Martina insisted on carrying all her luggage. **She wouldn't let** me help her.

lesson.heading: Repeated actions in the past
lesson.text: You can also use **would** to talk about things that happened regularly in the past. With this meaning, would is similar to **used to**.

examples.text: When we were children, we lived by the sea. In summer, if the weather was fine, **we would** all get up early and go for a swim.
Whenever Richard was angry, **he would walk** out of the room.
Whenever Richard was angry, **he used to walk** out of the room.

lesson.text: If the situation is over and cannot change, use would have + past participle: *You would have liked it* (but you didn't see it).

exercises.prompt: You should go and see the film. I think ___ it.
exercises.explanation: You haven't seen it yet, so we imagine the situation: you'd enjoy it.

exercises.prompt: Why don't you go and see Clare? ___ very pleased to see you.
exercises.explanation: An imagined situation now: she'd be pleased if you went.

exercises.prompt: Each sentence on the right follows a sentence on the left. Match them.

pairs.left: I'd like to go to Australia one day.
I wouldn't like to live on a busy road.
I'm sorry your trip was cancelled.
I'm looking forward to going out tonight.
I'm glad we didn't go out in the rain.
pairs.right: It wouldn't have been very nice.

pairs.left: I'm not looking forward to the trip.

exercises.prompt: It's a pity you couldn't come to the party last night. ___ it.
exercises.explanation: It didn't happen, so we imagine the past: would have + past participle.

exercises.prompt: I ___ Lisa, but I didn't have her number.
exercises.explanation: The situation is finished and in the past, so we use would have (done).

exercises.prompt: We took a taxi home last night, but got stuck in the traffic. It ___ quicker to walk.
exercises.explanation: Walking didn't happen, so we imagine it in the past: would have been.

exercises.prompt: Laura is late, and you are surprised because of what she said before.
exercises.answer: She promised she wouldn't be late.
exercises.explanation: won't in direct speech becomes wouldn't after a past reporting verb.

exercises.prompt: I wonder why Steve hasn't called me. He promised ___.
exercises.explanation: 'I'll call you' becomes he'd call after promised.

exercises.prompt: I asked Amanda what had happened, but she ___ me.
exercises.explanation: somebody wouldn't do something = he or she refused to do it.

exercises.statement: There was a problem with the car yesterday morning. The car won't start.
exercises.explanation: The car wouldn't start. The refusal was in the past, so we need wouldn't, not won't.

exercises.prompt: We used to live next to a railway line. Every time a train went past, the house ___.
exercises.explanation: would + verb describes something that happened regularly in the past.

exercises.prompt: Why is would used in each sentence?

items.text: I'd love to live by the sea.
I don't know what we'd have done without their help.
Whenever Richard was angry, he would walk out of the room.
It would be nice to buy a new car, but we can't afford it.
It's a shame you didn't see the film. You would have liked it.
We would stay at the beach all day, playing in the sand.
